sources.title: The King James Version
sources.what_it_is: The King James Version of the Holy Bible -- the canonical English text this app reads, cites, and builds every other layer around.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into verses-kjv.json and canon.json: the book/chapter/verse structure and the verse text itself, obtained via the scrollmapper/bible_databases project. Every other translation this app carries rides alongside this text; none ever replaces it.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Geocoding
sources.what_it_is: Place-coordinate data for the locations named throughout Scripture, from OpenBible.info's Bible-Geocoding-Data project.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into places.json, giving mapped places their coordinates on the World page.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Cross-References
sources.what_it_is: A cross-reference dataset connecting related passages across the whole Bible.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into cross-refs.json, powering the reader's own cross-reference lookups.

sources.title: KJV Red-Letter Markup
sources.what_it_is: A words-of-Christ annotation layer tracing back to Louis Klopsch's 1901 red-letter edition, obtained through eBible.org's own public-domain KJV OSIS distribution (via the seven1m/open-bibles collection).
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into SpokenBy/SpokenAt graph edges and data/compiled/red-letter-spans.json, which color Christ's own words wherever verse text renders in the reader. An annotation over our own KJV text, never a change to it.

sources.title: brain-fuel/bible Parallel Editions
sources.what_it_is: Six further public-domain Bible editions: the Clementine Vulgate, the Westminster Leningrad Codex, the Douay-Rheims (Challoner), Biblia 1776, Karl XII:s Bibel (1703), and the Greek Textus Receptus.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled as additional translation layers in the graph, alongside -- never replacing -- this app's own canonical KJV text.

sources.title: Theographic Bible Metadata
sources.what_it_is: A rich, hand-built dataset of biblical people, places, and events with dates, by Robert Rouse.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into events.json and much of places.json -- the great majority of this app's dated, narrative content rests on this dataset.

sources.title: Robertson's Harmony of the Gospels
sources.what_it_is: A.T. Robertson's A Harmony of the Gospels for Students of the Life of Christ (1922), which orders and groups the four Gospels' own parallel accounts.
sources.what_we_built: Robertson's own section numbers, titles, and groupings guided event-witnesses.toml's parallel-witness groupings and Passion Week's own chronological order. Every displayed event title and verse citation is this project's own, provenance-tagged (robertson_section) back to the section that grounded it.

sources.title: Crockett's Harmony of Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles
sources.what_it_is: William Day Crockett's A Harmony of the Books of Samuel, Kings and Chronicles (1897).
sources.what_we_built: Crockett's own section groupings guided the parallel-witness rows connecting Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles (and their related passages). Every displayed event title and verse citation is this project's own.

sources.title: Ussher's Annals of the World
sources.what_it_is: James Ussher's The Annals of the World (1658), a chronology of biblical and ancient history.
sources.what_we_built: Two of its own paragraph-numbered entries grounded two chronology-anchors.toml year values: Ezra's return, and the completion of Nehemiah's wall.

sources.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary
sources.what_it_is: M. G. Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), describing who and what the people and places of Scripture are.
sources.what_we_built: Its own entries fill the description shown on Place, Person, and PeopleGroup cards throughout the app, delivered via the already-vendored Theographic bundle.
sources.license: Public domain (carried in the vendored Theographic bundle, itself CC BY-SA 4.0)

sources.title: Kretzmann's Popular Commentary of the Bible
sources.what_it_is: Paul E. Kretzmann's Popular Commentary of the Bible (Concordia Publishing House, 1921-1924) -- verse-by-verse commentary across the whole Bible.
sources.what_we_built: Kretzmann's own commentary prose (never the KJV text his own commentary quotes) is compiled into verse-anchored commentary entries throughout the reader. A tentative date-mining pass over that same prose also surfaces the B.C./A.D. years Kretzmann mentions (data/exports/kretzmann-chronology.json, honestly marked tentative-extraction -- a future curatorial pass, not this app's chronology of record, adjudicates real placements from it).

sources.title: Luther's Small Catechism
sources.what_it_is: Martin Luther's Small Catechism -- the Ten Commandments, the Creed, the Lord's Prayer, and the Sacraments -- in the 1921 Bente-Dau English translation (Triglot Concordia / Concordia Triglotta).
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into catechism.json, in Luther's own words, with verse links drawn from Luther's own citations and from the mapping below.

sources.title: The Book of Concord
sources.what_it_is: The Lutheran church's confessional writings, in the same 1921 Bente-Dau translation as the Small Catechism above.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into the graph as a second full reading corpus alongside Scripture, paragraph by paragraph.

sources.title: Catechism Verse Mapping
sources.what_it_is: A mapping of Scripture references to Small Catechism questions, from the brain-fuel/catechism project, used here by the project owner's own direction.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into catechism.json's own per-question verse links, connecting the Catechism to Scripture throughout the reader.
sources.license: No license file -- used by the project owner's own explicit direction

sources.title: Catechism Reflection Questions
sources.what_it_is: 165 hand-authored teaching prompts across all 33 Small Catechism items, tiered child/youth/adult and ordered easy to difficult.
sources.what_we_built: Written for this project and compiled into catechism.json, so a lesson carries its own questions rather than leaving a teacher to invent them at 8am.

sources.title: Catechism Song Bindings
sources.what_it_is: A curated pairing of hymns to catechism items -- links and our own note on why each pairing fits. No audio, no recording, and no hymn text is redistributed here.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into catechism.json so a lesson can offer a hymn alongside the item it belongs to; playback is handed to the linked provider at runtime.
sources.license: CC0 1.0 Universal as to the CURATION (which hymn pairs with which item)

sources.title: Esri World Shaded Relief
sources.what_it_is: The label-free, light-terrain basemap tiles behind the World page's map -- relief, coastlines, and water tone, with every label of our own drawn on top.
sources.what_we_built: Fetched live by the browser from Esri's own servers at runtime -- never stored or redistributed by this app -- attributed on the map itself and here, verbatim: "Copyright:(c) 2014 Esri".

sources.title: Carto Basemap Tiles
sources.what_it_is: A fallback set of basemap tiles, used only if the Esri tile service is unreachable.
sources.what_we_built: Fetched live by the browser at runtime, the same as Esri above -- never stored or redistributed by this app.

sources.title: Leaflet
sources.what_it_is: The open-source JavaScript map library that renders the World page.
sources.what_we_built: Vendored and committed at client/wwwroot/vendor/leaflet/ (v1.9.4, upstream copyright banner retained), so a fresh clone runs without any fetch step.

sources.title: Our Own Curated Work
sources.what_it_is: Everything this project authored directly: the historical polity borders, the coastline land mask, biblical landmarks, narrative threads, eras, and the titles, sectioning, and aliases that connect it all together.
sources.what_we_built: Hand-authored under data/curated/ and compiled into narratives.json, eras.json, books-meta.json, landmarks.json, polities.json, and land-mask.json. Every displayed event title is this project's own phrasing, provenance-tagged (robertson_section, acts_section, kjv_superscription, theographic, atlas_section) back to whichever source above grounded it, so the mapping stays auditable.
